children: Shares of wires and cables companies came under sharp selling pressure on September 4 after UltraTech Cement launched its Ultravolt wires and cables business, intensifying competitive concerns in a segment dominated by established players such as Polycab India, KEI Industries and RR Kabel.

KEI Industries was among the hardest hit, falling 6.35 percent to Rs 4,989 in morning trade, while smaller player V-Marc India declined 5.94 percent to Rs 328. Larger rival Polycab India dropped 3.75 percent to Rs 8,477.50. R R Kabel fell 3.43 percent to Rs 2,528; Finolex Cables was down 1.98 percent at Rs 1,238.90, while Universal Cables slipped 0.66 percent to Rs 1,616.10. Havells India stock too was down 2.7 percent at Rs 1,167.

UltraTech shares, meanwhile, gained 0.6 percent to around Rs 11,343 in morning trade. The stock has fallen 4.8 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 8.6 percent decline in the Nifty 50. Its market capitalisation stood at just under Rs 3.34 lakh crore.

The selloff in rival cables and wires stocks followed Aditya Birla Group's formal entry into the market through UltraTech Cement, which has committed Rs 1,800 crore to the new business. The Ultravolt launch has come ahead of the company's earlier timeline and with an aggressive ambition to become one of India's top two wires and cables players within five years.

Brokerages were positive on UltraTech's execution and the scale of its ambitions. Morgan Stanley maintained an 'Overweight' rating with a target price of Rs 14,700, implying over 30 percent upside from the previous close.

The brokerage noted that UltraTech launched Ultravolt ahead of its earlier December-end timeline and had already spent around Rs 890 crore as of June against the total budgeted investment of Rs 1,800 crore. Morgan Stanley said the early launch and pace of capital expenditure pointed to strong execution, while it awaited further details as the business ramps up.

Jefferies maintained a 'Buy' rating on UltraTech with a target price of Rs 14,065. It highlighted that the company had entered the wires and cables business just 18 months after announcing the plan and said its positioning appeared more aggressive than initially expected.

Jefferies estimates that, once scaled up, the wires and cables business could contribute 3-7 percent of UltraTech's FY30 revenue and EBITDA, an opportunity that is not yet incorporated into its estimates. It also sees the venture complementing UltraTech's broader building-solutions strategy and the Aditya Birla Group's expansion into paints through Grasim Industries.

Ultravolt will initially focus on wires and low-tension cables, with manufacturing anchored at UltraTech's Jhagadia facility in Gujarat. The company plans a pan-India rollout covering more than 500 districts and 6,000 pin codes, with a target of reaching over one lakh retailers. It will also leverage more than 5,000 UltraTech Building Solutions outlets and over 20 warehouses.
The company has said Ultravolt will be the second-largest player in the wires segment by capacity at launch, underlining the potential competitive challenge for incumbent manufacturers.
